Subject: Horizon RFI: Dedicated inference reservation questionnaire

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking our call yesterday. I attached our procurement RFI — the team is specifically asking for granular answers on GPU families you support, expected per-GPU throughput (for our 512-token average prompt), reservation sizing methodology, and how burst capacity/fallbacks work.

Key asks:
- Recommended GPU mix for a 50k daily active user ML feature (expected 120k requests/day, avg payload 512 tokens).
- Per-GPU throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec at p95 tail targets).
- How you map customer SLAs to reservation commitments (baseline commit vs burst).
- Price delta for committed vs on-demand and any monthly "burst credit" allowances.

Can you return a short written response and a simple slotting workbook we can use in procurement? We need this by EOD Friday so legal and finance can start the review.

Attachments: Horizon_RFI_20271019.pdf (PDF)

Best,
Elena Morales

Horizon Health

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, contracts@horizonhealth.com

Subject: Re: Horizon RFI: Dedicated inference reservation questionnaire

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. Our answers below (high level) plus an attached slotting workbook and a short PDF summary. Happy to run a 60‑minute sizing workshop to validate assumptions.

Executive summary (short):
- Recommended committed footprint: start with a conservative 12 H100-equivalent slot baseline (committed), with a 2x burst guardrail to cover peak traffic.
- GPU mix recommendation: H100 (dense generative lanes) + A100-80GB (mixed workloads / long sequences) + L4 (low-cost embedding/transform inference). We express reservation in "slot units" (see workbook).

Throughput assumptions (512 token average prompt):
- H100 (H100-PCIe / H100-SXM): ~3200 requests/sec @ batch=32 and ~160k tokens/sec sustained per GPU for 512-token workloads when using continuous batching and KV caching. p95 tail latency < 250 ms for streaming small responses (under our batching SLOs).
- A100-80GB: ~1800 requests/sec @ batch=24 and ~92k tokens/sec sustained; better for models with larger context or memory-heavy KV cache needs. p95 tail ~300 ms.
- L4-class (edge/embedding): ~4500 requests/sec for short embeddings/200-token payloads; for 512-token generative requests L4 is not recommended.

Mapping SLA -> reservation (decision rationale):
- Latency-sensitive production (p95 < 300 ms): prioritize H100 slot commitments for predictable tail behavior.
- Throughput-sensitive but tolerant of slightly higher tail: A100-80GB slot commitments.
- Embeddings/bulk async workloads: L4 reserved pools.

Reservation model & burst policy: 
- Baseline commit expressed in slot units (X H100-equivalent slots). We convert A100 and L4 capacity to equivalent slot units in the workbook (A100=0.55 H100-eq, L4=0.12 H100-eq) to simplify billing.
- Burst: customers receive monthly burst credits equal to 100% of baseline for short-duration spikes, and an autoscale-on-demand pool billed at on-demand rates beyond credits.
- Fallbacks: We provide automated model variant fallbacks (quantized 4-bit flavor) with live routing; when dedicated pool is saturated we route non-latency-critical traffic to burst-on-demand or to lower-quantization model variants with explicit degradation profiles.

Pricing & tiers:
- Committed rate: 35% discount vs on-demand for H100-equivalent slots at the 12-slot baseline. Deeper discounts for 6, 12, 24 month terms (tiered).
- Burst-on-demand billed at on-demand list price; monthly credits cover short peaks.

Operational safeguards & SLAs:
- We guarantee 99.5% availability for dedicated pool, with automatic failover to cross-region pool per policy.
- Token-level cost and latency dashboards, per-route tracing, and rollback/canary tooling included.

Deliverables attached: slotting_workbook-v1.xlsx (mapping sheet, scenario tabs), redwood-rfi-response-20271019.pdf (one-page summary).

Open items we recommend validating in the workshop:
1) Confirm expected qps distribution across hours (we assumed 120k req/day with 15% peak hour).
2) Confirm tail latency SLOs for interactive cases vs async (embeddings).
3) Agree on the committed term length to finalize discounting.

Proposed next step: 60-minute workshop Thursday or Friday; I can run through the workbook and produce a formal SOW for signature.

Thanks — attaching the two files.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
